correctness.rationale: The Fourier-in-terminal-position backward resolvent solves (s+r-D∂xx)u=e^{ikx}+r u(ax) via coefficients r^n/product_{j=0}^n(s+r+D a^{2j}k²). Each inverse transform is an exact Laplace convolution. The first actual point-hitting Laplace transform equals the transition-density resolvent ratio; the stationary density is its pole residue. Global 1/2-Lipschitz convolution bounds control the s↓0 difference and ensure absolute geometric convergence. The independent convolution tail and E|Laplace|=1 yield explicit two-sided truncation errors. The Lyapunov drift and Brownian minorization ensure finite mean hitting. 87 finite numeric checks verify inverse Fourier, source Eq. (60), source Eq. (45) and enclosures, but do not replace the analytical proof.

originality.rationale: Biroli et al. Sec. III.2 explicitly leave kappa=T(-L/|a|) as numerical input in Eq. (60); the new theorem gives that constant and the entire full-line one-point hitting mean as explicit geometric series of finitely computable Laplace densities with certified truncation. The source stationarity product and point-resolvent identity are prior methods, not novelty. Pierce only sets nonnegative multipliers; Singh–Pal fixed-position resets. Bounded published-finding corpus searches and relevant source-comparison checks found no equivalent result. The closest own symmetric-interval exit result does not imply a single-point hitting law when discontinuous jumps cross without landing. General hitting-potential methods remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The original 2024 model reports the sign-reversing rescaling first-passage boundary value kappa as unknown without simulation. The exact all-initial-position elementary series and rigorous geometric intervals remove that obstruction, distinguishing a jump over the target from a true visit. The resolved natural physical observable is useful for controlled parameter and optimization studies and not merely a recomputation of the known stationary density. It is a scoped closure of an explicit literature gap, not an unsupported general breakthrough.
